initiative.title: Interactive data table explorer
initiative.summary: An adaptive, data-aware table that begins with an authored view and reveals field discovery, filtering, rich detail, and saved state in layers.

claims.statement: Create a detailed, evidence-backed handoff that several frontend UI tools can prototype independently.
sources: s12#hand it off to a number of different UI tools

claims.statement: Use the tool outputs to compare initial rendering, progressive disclosure, and meaningful design variance.
Adapt the table experience to row count, column count, data type, distribution, and the user's task.
sources: s02#ideal display depends on rows and columns

claims.statement: Treat very small tables as authored visual output rather than forcing an exploratory interface.
Start with a useful default and add controls only when they create clear value.
sources: s11#vast majority do not need fancy controls

claims.statement: Let users select visible columns and keep omitted columns discoverable.
sources: s03#control which columns are on screen
s03#interface to show what's been hidden

claims.statement: Support column labels, previews, reordering, direct resizing, and useful auto-sizing.
Horizontal overflow must remain visible and orient users to the fields outside the viewport.
sources: s03#unaware that the table has horizontal overflow

claims.statement: Format each data type well by default and keep raw values separate from display formatting.
sources: s03#common data type common data format

claims.statement: Keep rows compact while preserving an explicit path to full content.
sources: s11#text wraps to two or three lines maximum

claims.statement: Use the smallest detail surface that fits the content: hover card, popover, expansion, inspector, or modal.
sources: s06#on hover pop out a little card

claims.statement: Render lists and related objects as coherent cell summaries instead of spreading sparse repeated values across many columns.
Offer a compact global search that updates immediately and marks exact matching text.
Search only user-meaningful values and disclose matches in hidden fields.
Do not present fuzzy matches as precise filter results without explaining their ranking and scope.
sources: s11#normal business applications do not want fuzzy

claims.statement: Represent all active filters as one coherent query while allowing several editing surfaces.
sources: s08#choosing how to let the user see the query

claims.statement: Use numeric range controls instead of requiring exact text entry.
Use direct toggles for low-cardinality categories and disclose the remaining values for medium cardinality.
Show uniqueness, null rate, cardinality, and distributions when these facts help users choose fields or filters.
Use distributions as direct filters only when their scale and precision support the user's likely selection.
sources: s08#back it up with text inputs

claims.statement: Date filters must follow natural time boundaries and distinguish sliding durations from calendar periods.
sources: s09#this month this year this quarter

claims.statement: Date and time filters must use explicit time-zone semantics and produce the same result on server and client.
Sorting must include ascending, descending, and return-to-default states.
Identifiers with numeric parts must use natural rather than lexical sort order.
sources: s11#run one run eight run nine run ten

claims.statement: Do not put multi-column sorting in the standard business-table experience.
sources: s11#do not need a multi-column sort

claims.statement: Preserve all user-configured view state and reproduce it after refresh or sharing.
Store compact view state in the URL first, then use named workspace views when state becomes too large or contextual.
Autosave must remain visible and must not silently overwrite a named checkpoint.
sources: s10#overriding the thing that they named

claims.statement: Keep authored default views few and meaningful while allowing users to name their own longer view lists.
sources: s11#only giving them meaningfully different slices
s11#user created it and named it

claims.statement: Formatting can inherit from category to variable to view, with clear local overrides.
Put formatting controls near the displayed value and show live results while the user changes them.
sources: s10#as close to the display as possible
s10#see the result while they're changing

claims.statement: Arbitrary input requires field discovery, type inference, samples, distributions, errors, and user correction before table configuration.
Do not let arbitrary-table support expand silently into a complete ETL or spreadsheet platform.
The first comparison prototype should use a known schema, fixed data, and serializable local state.
Tool comparisons need identical data, tasks, and state frames while allowing visual and interaction variants.

statements: Global search is less common in serious data work.
A global text filter is the bare minimum for many business tables.
conflicts.resolution: Use a compact global exact-substring search as the default. Add column-aware filters when filtering becomes a central task.

statements: Direct column resizing improves fit and user control.
conflicts.resolution: Permit bounded resizing, preserve explicit overflow signals, and never remove fields silently.

statements: Autosave can overwrite the named view the user intended to preserve.
conflicts.resolution: Autosave the working state, but keep named checkpoints explicit and visibly modified.

shape.appetite: A detailed comparison brief and a high-fidelity, local prototype of one representative known-schema flow.
shape.problem: Tables become either underpowered static reports or permanently complex grids because controls do not adapt to data and task.

recommended_shape.summary: One responsive table with default, exploration, and focused-detail layers.
recommended_shape.source_of_truth: A serializable TableViewState over fixed fixture data.
recommended_shape.valid_intermediate: Linked static or generated frames before a runnable implementation.
recommended_shape.rollback: Keep each concept separate and promote none until comparison review.

success_moves: Hold the data fixture, tasks, and required states constant across tools.
Require state variants instead of one polished hero screen.
Fix interaction semantics while allowing visual and layout variation.
Prove a known-schema flow before arbitrary data support.
Require tools to disclose omissions and invented behavior.

first_proof.question: Can users reach advanced controls without facing permanent complexity or losing their table context?
first_proof.artifact: Six linked core states plus two edge states for the same purchase-order fixture.
first_proof.decision_rule: A reviewer completes five tasks without coaching and can always state what data is shown.

open_decisions: Side inspector versus inline row expansion for primary detail
Left field rail versus top command surface for exploration

fast_local_loop.workflow: Open each required state directly with fixed fixture data.

milestones.title: Comparable prototype concepts
milestones.outcome: Three to five comparable tool outputs from one fixture and task set.
milestones.proof: Score every output against the shared comparison scorecard.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: A reviewable concept set with assumption logs.
milestones.rollback: Discard any concept without affecting the source brief.

milestones.title: Runnable local interaction
milestones.outcome: The selected disclosure flow works against fixed local data.
milestones.proof: Complete the five review tasks and reproduce every preset state after refresh.
milestones.rollback: Keep alternative concepts and revert to the static comparison set.

milestones.title: Data-type and disclosure contract
milestones.outcome: Text, numeric, category, date, and rich values behave consistently.
milestones.proof: Run deterministic edge states and accessibility checks.
milestones.rollback: Disable advanced controls by field capability.

milestones.title: Responsive reference implementation
milestones.outcome: The selected concept retains state and information access at narrow widths.
milestones.proof: Verify desktop, narrow desktop, keyboard, and reduced-motion flows.
milestones.valid_intermediate_state: A frontend-ready reference without production services.
milestones.rollback: Fall back to the wide layout with explicit overflow mode.

open_decisions.question: Which primary detail surface retains context best?
open_decisions.evidence: Compare inline expansion and side inspector during task four.
open_decisions.fallback: Responsive side panel that becomes a bottom sheet.

open_decisions.question: Where should field exploration live?
open_decisions.evidence: Compare scan speed and remaining table width for left rail and top surface.
open_decisions.fallback: Collapsible left rail on desktop and full-screen sheet on mobile.

history.event: Recovered the June 25–29 interactive-table source set and completed intent, shape, and proof-first planning artifacts.
